History of Present Illness:
Patient is a ___ year old male with a history of cryptogenic 
cirrhosis, GERD, and esophageal dismotility who presents with 
altered mental status.
.
He was wintering in ___ with his family two weeks ago, and 
sought care at a hospital for emesis in the setting of a large 
fast food meal.  Records are not available for review, but per 
the family, the patient was given antibiotics.  Thought was 
given to a paracentesis, but the family states that the OSH did 
not feel comfortable with doing a para with the amount of 
ascites present.  Head CT was obtained given concern for slurred 
speech, which the family believes was unremarkable.  The patient 
was discharged from this ___ hospital a week ago today, and 
felt well.
.
Patient and family report that patient had ammonia level checked 
at ___'s office on ___, which was improved from prior.  
Patient was then told that he could stop taking lactulose.  
Patient then became more confused and lethargic last night and 
this morning, and patient was brought to ___ ED by family 
given concern for confusion.  The patient denies fevers, 
abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting.  He does note constantly being 
cold.  He reports feeling constipated last night, having 
difficuly removing his bowels.  He does report general malaise 
over the past month, and feels tired constantly.  He notes about 
a  12 pound weight loss since starting the diuretics.  No chest 
pain, no orthopnea, no PND, no dyspnea.  No recent alcohol use.
.

family confirmed that the patient's mental status had improved 
after he moved his bowels in the ED following lactulose

requesting dinner.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old male with cryptogenic cirrhosis, GERD, and 
esophageal dysmotility who presented to the ED with altered 
mental status, which has since resolved since lactulose 
administration. 
.  
# Encephalopathy- Patient likely encephalopathic at presentation 
in the ___ ED due to stopping lactulose.  Patient was not 
encephalopathic on the floor, nor throughout his hospital 
course.  Had low suspicion for SBP given lack of fevers, benign 
exam, and resolution of encephalopathy with lactulose.  Per 
family and patient report, patient has never had SBP in the 
past.  Non-focal neuro exam.  Continued lactulose 30 cc TID.  
Diagnostic paracentesis was performed, no evidence of SBP.  
Total protein from peritoneal fluid was 0.9, SBP prophylaxis was 
not started at discharge, can be re-considered at outpatient 
follow up.  Lactulose 30 cc TID was continued upon discharge.
.  
# Cirrhosis- cryptogenic.  decompensated, given recent 
encephalopathy and hypervolemia.  MELD score is 21.  Synthetic 
dysfunction persists.  Overall, LFTs actually improved over past 
month since patient first met Dr. ___ in early ___.  
Patient has abstained from alcohol.  Patient has grade I 
varices, no indication for variceal bleed prophylaxis, and 
nadolol was discontinued.  Abdominal ultrasound was notable for 
moderate ascites, but report did not specify location, and 
bedside ultrasound at time of paracentesis did not show a 
significant amount of ascites in the paracolic gutters.  In the 
future, the patient may benefit from ___ paracentesis, as 
only a small amount of peritoneal fluid was removed for the 
diagnostic paracentesis.  Furosemide and spironolactone were 
continued at home doses.  IgG was added on to labs, ___.  
Patient was advised to continue lactulose, and to only use 
hydroxyzine as needed for pruritis.  He is scheduled to see Dr. 
___ on ___.  
.
# Hyperkalemia- no ECG changes.  Resolved with lactulose and 
bowel movements.
.
# Elevated creatinine- 1.3, up from 1.1 one month ago.  
Urinalysis did not show any evidence of infection.  Home 
diuretics were continued, will need to have close follow up as 
an outpatient.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Patient with altered mental status.  Assess for pneumonia.

COMPARISONS:  None available.

FINDINGS:

The lung volumes are low.  There is no pleural effusion, focal consolidation
or pneumothorax.    Hilar and mediastinal silhouettes are normal.  The heart
is of normal size.  The pulmonary vasculature prominent and is suggestive of
intersitial edema.

IMPRESSION:
Prominent pulmonary vasculature, consistent with interstitial pulmonary edema.

INDICATION:  Patient with cirrhosis.  Assess for ascites and patency of the
portal vein.

COMPARISONS:  None available.

FINDINGS:

Liver is of heterogeneous  echotexture and demonstrates irregular contours,
compatible with cirrhosis.  No distinct hepatic lesion is identified.  There
is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  The
CBD is of normal caliber measuring 5 mm.  The main portal vein is patent
demonstrating hepatopetal flow.

The gallbladder wall appears mildly thickened.  Small amount of sludge is seen
within the gallbladder.  There is no ___ sign to suggest cholecystitis. 
The visualized pancreas appears unremarkable, its tail obscured by overlying
bowel gas.  Intra-abdominal aorta is of normal caliber.  The left kidney
measures 11.2 cm and the right kidney measures 10.2 cm.  There is no evidence
of renal masses, hydronephrosis, or nephrolithiasis.  The spleen measures 12.6
cm and appears normal.  There is moderate amount of ascites.

IMPRESSION: 
1)  Moderate amount of ascites.
 
2)  Heterogeneous echotexture of the liver compatible with cirrhosis.  No
distinct hepatic lesion is identified.  The main portal vein is patent.
 
3)  Mild thickening of the gallbladder wall with sludge.  No ___ sign to
suggest cholecystitis.
